A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 31-page versions of Infrastructure for AI Agents. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching substantive content, figures, tables, and references. Neither PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: v2 presents conceptual infrastructure proposals, illustrative scenarios, and research questions. Empirical examples are attributed to prior work; no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: v3 presents the same conceptual research agenda. Its tables and figures explain infrastructure categories and relationships, and it reports no original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The nine infrastructure proposals summarized in Table 1 and described in Sections 3–5 are unchanged. The abstract revision introduces no new component or procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for original training or evaluation. The illustrative application domains and hypothetical company example in Section 2.2 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. The discussions of existing alternatives throughout Sections 3–5 are identical.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports an original experimental protocol. No evaluation metrics, splits, training budgets, model configurations, or testing procedures are added or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. The hypothetical company example and other illustrative analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports original repeated-run statistics, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: No numerical results or qualitative findings are added, removed, or corrected. The cited observations and conceptual content of Tables 1–2 remain identical.

T1.justification: Definitions of agents, agent instances, and infrastructure remain unchanged. No formal mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions argue for external agent infrastructure and retain the same attribution, interaction, and response contributions. The abstract's explicit reference to heterogeneous agents clarifies the existing motivation without changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: The use-case arguments, adoption considerations, and limitations in Sections 3–6 are identical. The revised abstract restates the existing rationale for infrastructure rather than introducing a new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Technical descriptions and access information are unchanged. No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware details, or code/data resources are added or removed; the deleted OpenReview notice concerns review provenance.

R1.justification: Section 7, citations throughout the body, and all bibliography entries are unchanged. The relationship to earlier agent infrastructure and governance research is retained.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the opening motivation in the abstract, removes venue and OpenReview notices, and updates the arXiv version/date text. Sections 1–8, acknowledgments, and references retain their wording and organization.

P2.justification: v3 removes the repeated venue header and first-page review notice, shifting and reflowing the abstract. Figures 1–4, Tables 1–2, and the body layout on pages 2–31 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The abstract more explicitly identifies heterogeneous-agent interactions as motivation, but the framework, supporting arguments, limitations, and references remain identical. This limited editorial refinement and the publication-format changes do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
